name: MEDALLION FINANCIAL CORP

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The counter is that I have now talked myself out of the same name twice, on two different grounds, and that pattern deserves suspicion. First I dismissed it on a book-value error that turned out not to exist; now that the arithmetic has survived, I am dismissing it on input sensitivity instead. Medallion genuinely earns high returns on tangible equity, genuinely trades at 1.13x that equity, and has genuinely delivered $55.1M, $35.9M and $43.0M of net income across three years. If the ROTCE is real at even 18% — the LOW end of the observed range, not the mean — the justified multiple is still well above 1.13x and the stock is cheap. 'The inputs are uncertain' is a reason for low conviction, not a reason for no verdict.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Credit performance in the recreation lending book through a consumer slowdown — net charge-offs and 30+ day delinquency trend over the next two to three quarters. That is what decides whether the 17.9%-32.1% range is cyclical noise around a high-teens sustainable return, or the top of a credit cycle about to mean-revert below it.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Not yet, and that is the honest answer. I did not read the Q2 release or the 10-Q credit tables, so I have not seen the current delinquency trend. That is a limit I am recording rather than filling. What IS visible and does support the counter: three consecutive profitable years and a tangible book figure I have now verified twice. The counter has genuinely moved me from 'this gap is an artifact' to 'this gap is real but I cannot size it' — which is a different and weaker dismissal than the one I published this morning.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether the sustainable ROTCE is nearer 18% or 32%, which is the entire valuation; the current credit trend in the consumer books; and whether a 0.62 beta measured on $901K of daily volume means anything at all for the cost of equity.

what_changed: CORRECTION TO THE VERDICT RECORDED EARLIER TODAY. The first pass on this name asserted that the model overstated tangible book by 71% — that its $10.46 per share included $99.4M of non-controlling interest and the true figure was $6.13, making actual P/TBV 1.93x rather than 1.13x. That was wrong, and I have since verified it against the filing. Medallion's 30 June 2026 10-Q balance sheet reads 'Total stockholders' equity 408,617' with 'Non-controlling interest in consolidated subsidiaries 99,429' listed SEPARATELY BELOW it, summing to 'Total equity 508,046'. The SEC companyconcept endpoint confirms the extractor took us-gaap:StockholdersEquity, whose standard label is 'Stockholders' Equity Attributable to Parent', at exactly the $408,617,000 the model holds. The non-controlling interest was never inside the number, so deducting it would have understated tangible book by 41% rather than correcting it. The model's $10.46 and its 1.13x actual P/TBV are right. On the company itself: a 2026-08-05 10-Q and a 2026-07-29 8-K carrying Q2 results, plus June 8-Ks under items 5.02 and 8.01. No company news in the 90-day store, which is a fact about coverage rather than about the company.
consensus_case: At $11.82 against $10.46 of tangible book, Medallion Financial trades at 1.13x tangible common equity while the model computes a justified multiple of 3.54x from a 22.6% sustainable ROTCE against an 8.2% cost of equity. The market is refusing to pay that, and the refusal is not obviously wrong. The 22.6% is an average of three years running 17.9% to 32.1%, which is too wide a spread to call sustainable; the business is a subprime-adjacent consumer lender (recreation vehicles, home improvement) heading into a softening consumer; 41% of reported book is goodwill and intangibles; and the legacy taxi-medallion book is a reminder of what happens to this balance sheet when a collateral class reprices. A buyer at 1.13x tangible book is paying for earnings they do not believe repeat at 22.6%.
base_case_rationale: This is a book-method name, so no FCFF growth applies. Having removed the tangible-book error I claimed and found it was not there, the +213% gap is not explained away by a balance-sheet artifact and has to be judged on its merits — so I judged it, and I still do not think it is a thesis. The gap is manufactured almost entirely by the justified multiple, and that multiple is a Gordon-style ratio (ROTCE − g) / (COE − g) which is violently sensitive to both inputs. The ROTCE input is an average of 17.9%, 32.1% and the year between; the engine's own unstable_rotce flag fires on exactly that spread. Choosing the low end of the observed range instead of the mean drops the justified multiple by more than half and closes most of the gap without touching anything else. The cost of equity is 8.2%, which is low for a subprime-adjacent lender and reflects a 0.62 measured beta on a $271M name trading $901K a day — a beta I do not trust for a stock this thin, and one that flatters the multiple directly. A valuation whose answer moves from 'triple' to 'roughly fair' on two defensible input choices is not a valuation, and per the standing lesson about gaps that flip inside the band, conviction is capped low regardless.
key_risks: Sustainable ROTCE is an average of a 17.9%-32.1% range; the low end alone closes most of the gap
Subprime-adjacent consumer lending (recreation, home improvement) into a softening consumer
Goodwill and intangibles are 41% of reported book
$901K average daily dollar volume — a position could not be exited quickly, and the 0.62 beta driving the cost of equity is measured on that tape
Legacy taxi-medallion exposure is the standing reminder of what a collateral reprice does here
watch_for: Net charge-offs and 30+ day delinquency in the recreation and home improvement books over the next two to three quarters
A ROTCE print near the low end of the range, which would confirm the mean is not sustainable
Any change in Medallion Bank's preferred capital structure, which sits in the non-controlling interest
